asset_policy: dsl_primary_with_supporting_assets (creative track) — no supporting assets were used; every work is pure DSL
curatorial_statement: Twelve finished pieces, each built around a different *structure* rather than a different colour scheme: a night-possession time-space grid, a fermentation day curve, a generative botanical plate, an LED departure board, a circular seismograph drum, a 24-channel meter wall, a cross-stitch chart, a picture-book spread, a washi recipe card, a hand-engraved fingering chart, an ornamental playbill and a weekly tide matrix. The set is a study of what becomes possible once three measured DSL facts are known: the exact Transform placement rule, an honest text-width model, and the service's element/body/height budgets. Each piece also had to survive being looked at, so every work in this set carries at least one documented visual correction.

case_field_guide.request_ids: every render that used this case's DSL, in order
case_field_guide.review_evidence: iteration records that name a real image-view time

cases.title: Night possession plan · Line 4
cases.audience: Network Control Desk planners and protection officers at a (fictional) infrastructure operator
cases.use_context: Printed A3 desk sheet and a 1800 px screen view in a control room
cases.user_goal: See at a glance which track is closed, for how long, and where two possessions collide before the notice is issued
cases.content_basis: 8 possession windows, 5 work trains, 1 declared conflict; all times, headcodes and the operator are invented
cases.visual_intent: Dark control-room palette, 4 lane time-space diagram, amber rule, hatched possession bands, white train capsules with rotated chevrons
cases.dsl_capabilities: flat Stack absolute layout, rotated Transform bars (chevrons + conflict diamond), per-element alpha, keyed legend grid
cases.completion_criteria: every label readable at 50% zoom; no element covers another; the conflict mark sits in open space
cases.visual_review: v1 conflict diamonds were 112 px and covered the BALLAST band; v2-v4 moved the mark and shortened the callout; v5 verified by centroid measurement (conflict marker found at 1585,482 in open track space)
cases.fictional_disclosure: All subjects, brands, people, places, measurements and prices in this work are invented demo content for a DSL study; nothing depicts a real organisation or dataset.

cases.title: Sourdough fermentation schedule
cases.audience: Bakery team (4 people) at a fictional neighbourhood bakery
cases.use_context: A4 sheet pinned above the bench, also read on a phone
cases.user_goal: Follow today's steps and know what the dough should look like at each stage
cases.content_basis: 24 h dough and room temperature series and an 8 row step table; all values illustrative for a fictional bakery
cases.visual_intent: Warm linen paper, serif display type, hairline rules, filled dough band with a dashed room curve, on-curve annotation tags
cases.dsl_capabilities: rotated-bar polylines with round joins, stacked 2px area band, dashed line generator, measured text fitting, callout boxes clamped to the plot
cases.completion_criteria: curve never leaves the plot frame; callouts never cross the curve; table columns align
cases.visual_review: v1/v2 the dough curve read as disconnected dashes (abutting rotated bars only meet at corners on steep joints); v3 added joins and a filled band; v4/v5 nested clip layer re-based every child (abandoned, documented); v6 removed the alpha seam stripes and smoothed the series
cases.fictional_disclosure: All subjects, brands, people, places, measurements and prices in this work are invented demo content for a DSL study; nothing depicts a real organisation or dataset.
unresolved_issues: A true clip layer could not be used: nesting a Stack inside a clipped Container shifted every absolute child by the layer origin, so the series is clamped numerically instead.

cases.title: Generative botanical plate · Crypteris hallowayensis
cases.audience: Readers of a natural-history plate (museum wall, field guide spread)
cases.use_context: A3 portrait print, read at 40 cm and at thumbnail size
cases.user_goal: Show a plausible fern habit and its two magnified details with a proper specimen label block
cases.content_basis: procedurally generated frond, phyllotaxis inset (n=150, 137.5°), sporangia inset, collection data; the taxon is explicitly fictional
cases.visual_intent: Cream plate with a double frame, sepia serif type, one dominant organism, two circular insets, a scale bar and a caption
cases.dsl_capabilities: seeded PRNG geometry, log-spiral rachis, tapered pinnae from rotated bars, phyllotaxis from the golden angle, dashed guide ring, polygon-free circles
cases.completion_criteria: the plate reads as botanical rather than diagrammatic; insets do not collide; the caption sits inside the frame
cases.visual_review: v1 was rejected by the service twice (1 MiB body, then 4096 elements from rasterised pinnae); v2-v5 rebuilt the pinnae as rotated bars and moved the insets; v6 re-rendered after the entity fix so the collector line prints "R. Okonjo & T. Vasquez" instead of "&"
cases.fictional_disclosure: All subjects, brands, people, places, measurements and prices in this work are invented demo content for a DSL study; nothing depicts a real organisation or dataset.

cases.title: Dot-matrix departure board · Halloway Station
cases.audience: Passengers on platforms 3–4 of a fictional station
cases.use_context: A 1560 px LED board, also rendered small on a phone
cases.user_goal: Find the next departure, its platform and its status in under two seconds
cases.content_basis: 5 departures with destinations, platforms and states, plus a notice; the station, operator and timetable are invented
cases.visual_intent: Near-black board, amber/white/red LED cells, a hand-built 5x7 bitmap font, row banding, a status swatch legend
cases.dsl_capabilities: bitmap font emitted as square LED cells, per-status colour keys, monospaced column alignment, element budget management
cases.completion_criteria: every glyph legible; columns never collide; the board fits the element budget without dropping rows
cases.visual_review: v1 was rejected: 7381 elements against the 4096 cap; v2 revealed the local counter had under-reported by 2x (each Container is an element too); v3 fixed a column overlap; v4 tightened the panel
cases.fictional_disclosure: All subjects, brands, people, places, measurements and prices in this work are invented demo content for a DSL study; nothing depicts a real organisation or dataset.

cases.title: Drum seismogram · station HLY
cases.audience: A seismology duty officer reading an overnight record
cases.use_context: A wide sheet on a monitoring desk, also used as a print
cases.user_goal: See the P-wave onset, judge the coda, and read the event parameters
cases.content_basis: three radial drum traces, a 3 line helicorder, an event summary; the event, station and magnitudes are invented
cases.visual_intent: Smoked-paper dark ground, concentric rings with hour marks, green/blue/amber traces, a red onset marker, a helicorder panel
cases.dsl_capabilities: parametric circular geometry, polar helpers, multi-series waveforms, radial tick labels, dash control
cases.completion_criteria: the onset marker sits on the trace; no label collides; the helicorder shows quiet vs event
cases.visual_review: v1 traces were dashed (2.1° steps) and the STATUS row collided with the HELICORDER heading; v2 halved the step to 1.55° and moved the panel
cases.fictional_disclosure: All subjects, brands, people, places, measurements and prices in this work are invented demo content for a DSL study; nothing depicts a real organisation or dataset.

cases.title: Monitor wall · 24 channels
cases.audience: A mix engineer and a producer in a control room
cases.use_context: A 1760 px screen and a printed reference sheet
cases.user_goal: Compare channel levels and spot the channels that risk clipping
cases.content_basis: 24 named channels with levels and peak holds on a real dB scale; the session, names and levels are invented
cases.visual_intent: Dark console palette, 2.4 dB segments coloured by zone, white peak-hold caps with numeric values, a zone key
cases.dsl_capabilities: dB-to-pixel scale mapping, segmented bars, computed peak caps, dense monospace labelling
cases.completion_criteria: bar length is comparable across channels; every peak label is readable; no bar overlaps its neighbour
cases.visual_review: v1/v2 printed "&" and "<" in the zone key because entities are not decoded by the parser; v3 moved the legend to minus-sign wording and restored the true values

cases.title: Tide & light planner · Halloway Rowing Club
cases.audience: A coastal rowing club's coxswains and coaches
cases.use_context: A wall sheet in the boathouse, read before an outing
cases.user_goal: Choose the day and the hour: enough water, enough light, high water inside daylight
cases.content_basis: 7 day tide curves, 28 high/low water entries, daylight windows and moon phases; all predictions come from a two-constituent harmonic generator and are explicitly not for navigation

final_collection_review: Twelve works reviewed at full size and as a contact sheet. Independence check: no two works share a layout skeleton, and the shared code is limited to primitives (text fitting, rotated bars, area fills, legends). Size range 1080x1520 to 1920x1200; colour languages differ per work by design (control-room navy, linen paper, cream museum plate, black LED, smoked paper, console charcoal, woven flax, paper-collage brights, washi, white music paper, cream playbill, deep-water dark). Defects found and fixed in review are listed per case. Remaining known limits: a true clip layer is unusable with absolute positioning (see case-02 and technique-notes.md), and the element budget of 4096 caps generative density.
unresolved_issues: Clip layers cannot be combined with absolute positioning in this build: nesting a Stack inside a clipped Container re-bases every child by the layer origin.
The 4096-element cap limits procedurally dense sheets; workarounds are coarser scanlines and fewer motifs, which is a real constraint on generative density.
Text inside a width-constrained Container still wraps rather than truncating, so every string is measured before placement by design.
